# OpenCode Zen

Curated coding models. Its free models only work inside the OpenCode app (use the opencode agent for those); this API needs credits.

| | |
|---|---|
| Kind | Chat API (OpenAI-compatible): returns code that conductor applies |
| Cost | Paid, per token |
| Key | `OPENCODE_API_KEY` from https://opencode.ai/console (the provider's docs name no variable; this is conductor's name for it) |
| Endpoint | `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1` |
| Default model | picked automatically from the live list (coding models first); choose your own with `conductor models opencode-zen --all` |
| conductor name | `opencode-zen` |
| Privacy | Some models may use data for training. |
| Provider docs | https://opencode.ai/docs/zen/ |
| Checked | 2026-11 |

## Set up

1. Create an API key: https://opencode.ai/console
2. Add it to conductor. It asks for the key (hidden input), lets you pick a model, sends one test prompt and adds it to the `docs`, `test`, `review` and `ask` roles:
   ```bash
   conductor add opencode-zen
   ```
3. Check it any time:
   ```bash
   conductor doctor --live
   ```

Or click **Add** on its card in `conductor ui` → Providers.

## Without the wizard

Save the key (hidden input; or pipe it in):
```bash
conductor keys set OPENCODE_API_KEY
```

Then add this to `~/.config/conductor/config.json` (all projects) or `.conductor/config.json` (one project):
```json
{
  "providers": {
    "opencode-zen": {
      "enabled": true,
      "model": "<model id>"
    }
  }
}
```
List models: `conductor models opencode-zen --all`. Put `opencode-zen` in any role's chain in `conductor ui` → Roles & fallback.

The variable name only tells conductor where to find the key; the provider never sees it. To use a key you already keep under another name, set `"apiKeyEnv": "YOUR_VAR"` on `opencode-zen`.

## Troubleshooting

- **401 / 403**: the key is wrong, expired, or still a placeholder. Run `conductor keys` to see where it comes from, then `conductor keys set OPENCODE_API_KEY`.
- **404 or "model not found"**: the model id changed. Pick a current one with `conductor models opencode-zen --all`.
- **429**: rate limit. conductor puts the provider on cooldown and moves to the next one in the chain; `conductor cooldown --clear opencode-zen` resets it.
- **Empty reply**: some free routes return nothing now and then; conductor retries once, then falls back.
